clue.text: Fool taken back by school as planned

indicators.note: taken back tells us the word for fool is read from right to left

parts.note: to fool someone is to delude them

explanation.surface: A prank pulled on a pupil was all part of the school's plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' is a verb, not a person; 'taken back' gives EDULED, placed after the school abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done as planned happened on schedule, at its appointed time.

clue.text: Second date for Roman camps

parts.note: the Ides was a date in the Roman calendar, the 15th or 13th of the month

explanation.surface: A Roman legion pitching camp in time to fight a second engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camps' is a noun here: opposing groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing sides in a dispute are its camps, factions holding different views.

clue.text: The real England's freely set in opera

indicators.note: set freely means arranged with no fixed order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An opera staged in the authentic English countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansel and Gretel is an opera by Humperdinck, based on the fairy tale.

clue.text: Heartless devil that is sweet on the outside like Kipling's female

indicators.note: on the outside places the word for sweet around the other pieces

parts.note: dear means sweet or lovable

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of devil are removed, leaving its outside two

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A devil without feelings, sweetly disguised, recalls a line from Kipling.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling wrote that 'the female of the species is more deadly than the male'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's poem calls the female more deadly than the male, so the comparative fits.

clue.text: Drink in stories on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard, so the words for the stories are pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: a light tale is a light-hearted story, the kind of entertainment broadcast

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there is a drink in the stories they hear broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: said aloud, 'light tale' is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Light ale is a pale, low-strength bottled beer, a classic British pub drink.

clue.text: Limp around on one's uppers in yard

indicators.note: around turns the whole assembly the other way round
in places the poor word inside the yard abbreviation

parts.note: on one's uppers is a British idiom for very poor, with shoes worn through to the uppers

explanation.surface: Someone hobbles about the yard, down at heel and penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on one's uppers' is British slang for broke. 'around' turns YPOORD to read the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something droopy hangs down limply, lacking firmness or stiffness.

clue.text: Racing results this writer's seen in teachers paper

indicators.note: seen in places the setter's I'M inside the teachers' paper

parts.note: the TES, the ... Educational Supplement, is the British weekly paper for teachers
this writer is the setter, so this writer's = I'm, I am

explanation.surface: A newspaper for schoolteachers that also prints the horse-racing results.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints "teachers'" with an apostrophe. 'Paper' looks like the definition, since the answer is this very newspaper's name, but it belongs to TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing results are the recorded times, how long each runner took to finish.

clue.text: Member of choir winning series

definitions.meaning: a boy singer with the highest voice part in a choir
a run of three wins, as when a team takes three trophies in one season

explanation.surface: A chorister's choir on a run of competition victories.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble sings the top part; in sport, winning three trophies is a treble.

clue.text: Get high after handling small bull?

indicators.note: after places the word for reach the top behind the other pieces

parts.note: management is handling, the running of something
to peak is to reach the highest point

explanation.surface: A cowboy feels exhilarated after taming a little bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' is not the animal but bull, slang for pretentious nonsense; the question mark flags the jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: Management-speak is corporate jargon, often dismissed as empty nonsense or hot air.

clue.text: Turner's turning on one old American subversive

indicators.note: turning means the word for turners is read backwards

parts.note: a tide turns, so it is a turner; turner's here is turner is, tides
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An art critic reports Turner painting while sitting on an elderly American dissident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter, but it is a tide; TIDES turned is SEDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Seditious speech or conduct incites rebellion against authority, the very meaning of subversive.

clue.text: City that's half-hidden, with area guarded by witch

indicators.note: half of the following word is taken, here its second half
guarded by means surrounded by, so the area letter sits inside the witch

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch

explanation.surface: A town half-concealed from view, its district watched over by a witch: something from a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hidden' gives DEN, the back half of HIDDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Den Haag is the Dutch name for The Hague, the seat of the Netherlands government.

clue.text: Wacky comedian wanting maiden or nymph

indicators.note: wacky means crazy, so the remaining letters of comedian are scrambled
wanting means lacking, so the maiden letter is removed from comedian

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A zany comic wants either a young girl or a nymph to perform with.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M from COMEDIAN and rearrange the other seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oceanid is a sea nymph of Greek myth, a daughter of Oceanus.

clue.text: Appropriate quarter with shade

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
teal is a shade of greenish blue

explanation.surface: Choosing a fitting colour for one part of a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective but is the verb, to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it without permission, a synonym for pinching it.

clue.text: Best way to reach garret?

definitions.meaning: of the highest class or quality
a garret is an attic room, reached by climbing the highest set of stairs

explanation.surface: Asking how best to get up to an attic room.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means first-rate; literally, the top flight of stairs leads to the attic.

clue.text: Eastern Democrat stopping not long ago in high spirits

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the Democrat letter fills a space inside the word for recently

parts.note: lately means recently, not long ago
D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A Democrat from the East Coast who recently quit, apparently in a good mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something elatedly means doing it joyfully, full of excitement and happiness.

clue.text: Mad hatter's right about a woodland fungus

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the possessive hatter's supplies its S as a letter here
A is the abbreviation for about, as in approximately

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter is correct about a fungus he found in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad hatter' reads as Lewis Carroll's character, but 'Mad' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthstar is a woodland puffball whose outer layer splits into a star shape.

clue.text: Magazine articles show butterfly heading off to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going to the west means reading from right to left
heading off means the first letter is cut from the butterfly

parts.note: the comma is a British butterfly, named for a white comma-shaped mark on its wing

explanation.surface: A magazine runs pieces on a butterfly flying off westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' cuts COMMA to OMMA; 'to the west' turns that to AMMO. 'Magazine' is not a publication: it is the part of a gun that holds rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition is what a gun's magazine holds: the rounds or cartridges loaded into it.

clue.text: Change of fortune as poems do not appear entirely to have genuine context

indicators.note: context, used as surroundings, puts the word for genuine round the shortened poems

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: not appearing entirely means the last letter of the word for poems is lost

parts.note: verse means poems collectively, poetry

explanation.surface: A poet's fortunes change when the poems fail to appear in full in their genuine setting.
explanation.walkthrough: VERSE without its last letter is VERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal is a sudden turn for the worse, a setback in fortune.

clue.text: A game soldier, foremost in attack or defence

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: foremost in takes the first letter of the word attack

explanation.surface: A plucky soldier, always in the front line whether attacking or defending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A game soldier' reads as a brave soldier, but game here is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence of one's opinions or conduct.

clue.text: End of line after free trip

indicators.note: after places the final letter behind the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free (someone of something)

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of the word line

explanation.surface: Reaching the terminus after a journey that cost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride is a short journey or outing, a trip in a car or on horseback.

clue.text: Arrangement of pansies involving a thousand plants

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the thousand letter goes inside the rearranged flowers
an arrangement rearranges, so the letters of pansies are mixed up

parts.note: K, from kilo, stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A flower arranger puts together a display of a thousand pansies.
explanation.walkthrough: PANSIES rearranged gives SEAPINS, with K slipped in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea pinks, also called thrift, are low pink-flowered plants of coastal cliffs.

clue.text: Wound has upset key sports officials

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, reading them from the bottom up

parts.note: DEL is the delete key on a keyboard
the IOC is the International Olympic Committee

explanation.surface: An injury upsets the referees, a key match moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' is the past of wind (rhymes with found), not an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Wound in the sense of wrapped round in loops, as a rope or spring is coiled.

clue.text: Spanish district where one may drink port

parts.note: a bar is a place for drinking
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, Rio for short

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood in Spain where you can enjoy a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as the wine, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrio is a district or neighbourhood of a Spanish-speaking town.

clue.text: Wife leaving school and opening a spa

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the wife letter is removed from the school

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school
a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A woman quits her teaching job and opens a health spa.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROW without W gives HARRO. Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrogate grew famous for its mineral springs, an example of an English spa town.

clue.text: Drink provided by medical assistant

indicators.note: provided by indicates the letters are supplied by a run across these two words

explanation.surface: A nurse hands over a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of medicaL into ASSIstant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassi is a yoghurt-based drink from South Asia, served sweet or salted.

clue.text: Top one providing clue for Italian team

definitions.text: Top one providing clue for Italian team

parts.words: Top one providing clue for Italian team
parts.note: to top someone is to kill them, which leads to burying; and a clue meaning bury would also lead to Milan's football club

explanation.surface: The best person to set a puzzle about Italian football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like best, but here it is slang for kill; what follows a killing is burial, and the burial word is also the name of a Milan football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter Milan is a famous Italian team, and the club's name also means to bury the dead.

clue.text: Short emperor and fat duke left as figureheads

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the emperor's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Titus was a Roman emperor

indicators.note: left means departed, so the duke letter is taken from the fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A stunted emperor and a portly duke reign in name only.
explanation.walkthrough: TITUS shortened gives TITU; LARD without D gives LAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Titular rulers hold a title without real power, which is what figureheads do.

clue.text: Part with good pieces in collection

indicators.note: in puts the good and pieces letters inside the collection

parts.note: a set is a collection of things belonging together
chess or draughts pieces are called men

explanation.surface: Some good chess pieces belong to a collector's set.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one of the sections into which something divides, so a part of it.

clue.text: Cross man said to have easy life almost died

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the man is dropped

parts.words: man said to have easy life
parts.note: the life of Riley is the proverbial easy life
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An angry fellow who supposedly lived comfortably nearly died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The life of Riley' is an idiom for a carefree, comfortable life.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means annoyed or irritated, the adjectival sense of cross.

clue.text: At sea like tar on ship

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Out on the ocean, as a sailor aboard a vessel would be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tar' looks like a sailor, but it is fodder alongside LIKE and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil tanker is a ship built to carry oil in bulk.
